clinical_features.symptoms:
SYMPTOMS & SIGNS 
MUSCARINIC (“DUMBELS”) 
NICOTINIC 
CNS 
D – 
diaphoresis, diarrhoea 
U – 
urination 
M – 
miosis 
B – 
bradycardia, bronchorrhoea, 
bronchospasm 
E – 
emesis 
L – 
lacrimation 
S – 
salivation 
Fasciculations 
Weakness 
Hypertension 
Tachycardia 
Mydriasis 
Anxiety 
Ataxia 
Restlessness 
Confusion 
Convulsions 
Coma 
 
 
 
 
* Universal precautions 
IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT 
* Decontamination – remove clothing, wash patient with soap and water 
*  Supportive care of ABCs and general management principles of a poisoned 
patient (see protocol) 
Note: 
If intubation is required, avoid succinylcholine if possible (causes prolonged paralysis) 
 
 
 
 
 
** ATROPINE 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
- 
can be administered IM if no immediate IV access (100mg amps in resus, NB SECTION 21 FORM) 
- 
this only treats the muscarinic symptoms 
- 
May cause anticholinergic toxidrome at high doses – monitor closely. NB urine catheter 
STAT DOSE 
INFUSION (start once atropinised) 
0.04 - 0.05mg/kg IV (3 – 5mg adult) 
double every 5 minutes until atropinisation 
“escalating atropinisation” 
200mg Atropine in 200ml 0.9% NaCl (1mg/ml) 
Use a Dial-a-flow/Infusion pump  
10-20% of total dose already given/hr 
(total dose i.e. for escalating atropinisation) 
 
 
END POINT = CLEARING OF RESPIRATORY SECRETIONS (ATROPINISATION) (NOT based on tachycardia or pupil dilation) 
** SEIZURES 
- 
Check blood glucose 
- 
Use a benzodiazepine only – NO anticonvulsant agents 
- 
Clonazepam; Diazepam; Lorazepam 
** MONITOR & CORRECT ELECTROLYTE ABNORMALITIES. Consider MgSO4 4g/day (weak evidence) 
** WEAKNESS 
- look for signs of weakness (nicotinic symptom) 
- is the patient able to lift and hold their head up for 10 seconds; ask the patient to squeeze your hand 
- Intubation and supportive management is the only way to control weakness (respiratory failure) 
 
 
DISPOSITION 
Int Med Consultation
